title: Introduction to Information Retrieval
text: Information retrieval is the process of finding relevant documents in large collections.

title: Boolean Model
text: The Boolean model uses AND OR and NOT operators to match documents exactly.

title: Inverted Index
text: An inverted index maps terms to posting lists for fast search.

title: Phrase Search
text: Phrase queries require word positions in the inverted index.

title: Vector Space Model
text: The vector space model ranks documents using term weights and cosine similarity.

title: Web Search
text: Web search engines use crawlers indexes and ranking algorithms.

title: Probabilistic Model
text: The probabilistic model estimates the probability that a document is relevant to a query.

title: Evaluation Measures
text: Precision and recall are common evaluation measures in information retrieval.

title: Recommender Systems
text: Recommender systems suggest items to users based on preferences and interactions.

title: Dynamic Indexing
text: Dynamic indexing supports efficient document addition and deletion.

title: Merging Indexes
text: Large search engines periodically merge indexes to improve query performance.

title: Stop Words
text: Some systems remove very common terms before indexing documents.

title: Auxiliary Index
text: An auxiliary index stores newly added documents before the next merge.

title: Lazy Deletion
text: Lazy deletion marks removed documents in a deletion list instead of updating every posting list.

title: Boolean Phrase Queries
text: Boolean retrieval can be combined with exact phrase queries.

title: Disk Persistence
text: Saving and loading the index from disk avoids re indexing the whole collection.

title: Posting List Compression
text: Posting lists can be compressed to reduce disk space.

title: Query Parser
text: A query parser converts text queries into Boolean expression trees.
